If the customer appears dissatisfied with complaint outcome, check if a written response is required as per Knowhow.


If a written response is NOT required:

“I understand you’re not happy with <my apology/my response to your complaint> . If you would like, you can escalate the matter to AFCA.

You can contact them by calling 1800 931 678, emailing info@afca.org.au, or submitting a form on their website, afca.org.au. Thank you for your time today”

(END CALL)

*Written responses are required for hardship and insurance complaints – discuss with your People Leader


If a written response IS required:

“I understand you’re not happy with <my apology/my response to your complaint>. If you would like, you can escalate the matter to AFCA.

I’ll send you their details in our written response to your complaint. Thank you for your time today.”

(END CALL)


 

If customer is refusing a required written response (NO domestic violence concerns):

“I understand you don’t want a written response, however unfortunately ANZ has an obligation to send you a written response in this situation. It will include AFCA’s details so you can escalate further if you wish. Thank you for your time today.”

(END CALL)

 


If customer is refusing a required written response (domestic violence concerns and no alternative address available):

"We will not send you a written response however, the response will still be prepared and attached to your complaint, should you wish to receive it in the future. Thank you for your time today."

(END CALL)

 

If you need to end your call due to continuing inappropriate behaviour, see Customer Behaviour Escalations process in Knowhow. 


If your line manager is available to receive the call:

"I'm sorry I am not going to continue this conversation. I am going to transfer you to my line manager."


If your line manager is NOT available to receive the call:
"As you've continued to speak inappropriately, I'm now going to terminate this phone call."
(END CALL)
